title: angl
blurb: A small, keyboard-first macOS browser on the system WebKit, with tree tabs, isolated Containers, and plain-file config.
overview: Built in Swift 6 and AppKit on top of macOS's built-in WKWebView instead of bundling Electron or another engine. Includes a Rust Bitwarden SDK bridge, per-site JavaScript and ad-blocker controls, 120 Hz rendering on AC power, and out-of-process filter compilation so memory stays low (227 MB vs. Safari's 287 MB on Wikipedia). Signed and notarized for Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 15 or newer. GPL-3.0.
features: No URL bar by default, with floating tab switching and commands on Cmd+T and Cmd+K
Tree tabs, Spaces with isolated Containers, and live-reloaded JSON/CSS config
Per-site JavaScript, content blocker, dark mode, and volume controls
Bitwarden passkeys and login autofill via a Rust SDK bridge, plus Apple Passwords

title: winstream
blurb: A lean Windows 11 streaming and recording studio written in Rust on WGC, Direct3D 11, and NVENC, using ~3x less RAM and far less CPU than OBS.
overview: StreamApp's Windows counterpart, built as a Rust workspace with Windows Graphics Capture, Direct3D 11 compositing, direct NVENC 13.0 bindings, WASAPI per-process audio with RNNoise and K-weighted -14 LUFS leveling, and a std-only FLV muxer. Benchmarked against OBS 32.0.2 at 1080p60 NVENC H.264 (6000 kb/s, Ryzen 9 9950X3D, RTX 4090) with overlays and audio: 262 MB private RAM vs. OBS's 788-931 MB, 150 MB VRAM vs. 233-259 MB, +13% single-core CPU overhead under GPU-bound load vs. +37% for OBS with overlays, and stronger 1% and 0.1% lows under GPU-bound and uncapped loads (with A/V sync at -7.9 ms median). Capped 599 Hz 0.1% lows still trail OBS's DX game capture hook because of WGC composition overhead. Not public on GitHub yet.
features: ~262 MB active RAM (67 MB dormant) and 150 MB VRAM vs. OBS's 788-931 MB RAM and 233-259 MB VRAM
GPU-bound load: +13% single-core CPU and 205/201 fps (1%/0.1% low) vs. OBS + overlays at +37% CPU and 201/185 fps
Uncapped load: 802/748 fps (1%/0.1% low) vs. OBS + overlays at 680/621 fps
WASAPI per-app audio capture, RNNoise mic cleanup, K-weighted -14 LUFS loudness leveling, and separate VOD track
TOML scenes with cut/morph/wipe transitions, camera low-light shadow lift and denoise, and Twitch chat/alert overlays

title: Pace Bar
blurb: A macOS menu bar app for tracking Codex and Claude quotas, local inference, and OpenRouter credit.
overview: A fork of CodexBar by Peter Steinberger and contributors, built with SwiftUI and AppKit. The Apple Silicon download is signed and notarized for macOS 14 and up (Intel Macs can build from source). Forecasts are rough estimates, and it doesn't switch accounts.
features: One quota ring per Codex and Claude subscription
Pooled Codex forecast that flags quota about to reset unused
Local inference token counts and speed, with optional GPU readings
OpenRouter balance kept separate from estimated API cost

title: Inkjoin
blurb: An iPhone puzzle game where you fill in squares to make one connected shape, using the numbers as clues. Every solved puzzle turns into a drawing.

media.title: preview
media.alt: An Inkjoin puzzle being solved with a hint. Empty squares are marked with dots, and the finished shape becomes a drawing with a red stamp.
media.caption: Solving a 7x7 puzzle with one hint. The grid fades out and the finished drawing gets a red stamp.

overview: Nine chapters introduce one idea at a time, plus a new puzzle each day and practice at four difficulty levels. Every puzzle has one solution and never asks you to guess. Hints are unlimited with no penalty. Works offline on iPhone (requires iOS 26).
features: 74 puzzles across nine chapters
Daily puzzles that get harder through the week
Hints that show where to look, explain a step, and can fill it in
Solved puzzles saved as drawings

title: Herdwick
blurb: An iPhone and iPad app for herdr so you can check on and answer your coding agents over SSH.
overview: Connects to your own machine over SSH, lists every agent herdr is tracking, and renders their transcripts as chat threads, with a live terminal when you need it. Requires iOS 26 and a Mac or Linux host running herdr. Independent project, not affiliated with herdr or Tailscale.
features: Inbox of agents across hosts, with the ones waiting on you at the top
omp, Claude Code, and Codex transcripts shown as chat
Native controls for questions and permission prompts
Works over plain SSH or Tailscale, with no account or analytics

title: Dictation
blurb: A local voice-to-text app for Mac with custom vocabulary for technical terms, built on Handy.

media.title: preview
media.alt: The Dynamic Orb recording overlay: a dark glass capsule appears, a rainbow light ripples as you speak, a cursor pulls a drop from its edge that melts back, and the light swirls while transcribing.
media.caption: Dynamic Orb overlay: light ripples as you speak and swirls while transcribing.

overview: Built on Handy, with Fast and Accurate speech-recognition presets. Plain dictation runs completely offline once the models download. If you want text cleanup, you can point it at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The Apple Silicon download is signed and notarized.
features: Local speech recognition with Fast and Accurate presets
Custom vocabulary for the Accurate preset
Configurable dictation shortcuts
Optional transcript cleanup with a plain-text fallback

title: StreamApp
blurb: Record your screen or stream to Twitch from your Mac's menu bar.
overview: A Mac menu bar app for capturing your screen or windows, tweaking webcam and audio, streaming to Twitch, using a notch teleprompter, and drawing right on the desktop. Signed and notarized for Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 26 or newer (or build from source without a signing cert). Licensed under GPL-3.0.
features: Crash-recoverable screen and window recording
Desktop and Full Camera layouts with webcam punch-in
Twitch streaming with a confirmation step before going live
Desktop drawing and live loudness meters

title: Tablet Companion
blurb: Set up a Wacom tablet and its drawing shortcuts on your Mac.
overview: A small setup helper for the Wacom Intuos BT S (tested with driver 6.4.14-1). It walks through the Wacom driver install and maps tablet buttons to StreamApp drawing shortcuts without touching your other buttons. Only supports the Intuos BT S for now. Signed and notarized for Apple Silicon Macs on macOS 26 or newer.
features: Guided Wacom driver download and installer handoff
Suggested button layout for StreamApp drawing
Restore previous button mappings anytime
Local backups of your tablet settings

title: CenterSeat
blurb: A movie-seat finder that compares seat maps across showtimes to rank the best seats together.
overview: Compares open seats across nearby showtimes and ranks the best seats together so you don't have to click through every auditorium map yourself. Live searches need a configured data provider.
features: Compares seat maps across nearby showtimes
Ranks contiguous seats based on where you like to sit
Pluggable data provider for live showtime searches

title: Boilerplate
blurb: My macOS and Linux workspace setup, managed with chezmoi and mise.
overview: My shared dotfiles and workspace config for macOS and Linux, managed with chezmoi and mise. Includes bootstrap and recovery notes for bringing up a new machine.
features: Shared macOS and Linux configuration
Tool version management with mise
Machine-aware templates
Bootstrap and recovery notes

title: Jeopardy Study App
blurb: A Jeopardy study app for searching clues, drilling categories, and playing full boards.
overview: Search past Jeopardy clues, drill specific categories, or play through full boards with answer checking and progress tracking.
features: Clue search and category practice
Full-board game mode
Answer checking
Progress tracking

title: OpenCode Monitor
blurb: A small macOS menu bar app for keeping an OpenCode server under control.
overview: Puts OpenCode server status, start and stop controls, logs, updates, and optional idle shutdown right in your macOS menu bar.
features: Menu bar status and quick controls
Start, stop, and restart actions
Optional idle auto-stop
Build and uninstall scripts

title: btuckerc.dev
blurb: This website. A terminal-style portfolio with keyboard navigation, a command palette, and fuzzy project search.
overview: Built with React and Vite and styled like a terminal. All the project data lives in one JSON file, and every route prerenders to static HTML at build time.
features: Command palette on the colon key
Fuzzy project search that forgives typos
Keyboard navigation across lists
Theme and font switching

title: AudioReader
blurb: A local audiobook player with synced captions generated with Whisper.
overview: Plays local audiobooks in the browser alongside synced VTT captions generated locally with Whisper.
features: Synced VTT captions
HTML5 audio playback
Playlist support
Local Whisper transcription

title: Farkle Scorer
blurb: An offline iOS scorekeeper for Farkle with tap-to-score dice and some nearby multiplayer experiments.
overview: Tap the dice you rolled or enter scores manually if you're using physical dice. Supports custom house rules and an experimental nearby multiplayer mode.
features: Tap-to-score dice
Manual score entry for physical dice
Configurable house rules
Works completely offline

title: Flipping Seven Calculator
blurb: An iOS scorekeeper for Flip 7 with round history and undo.
overview: Keeps score for Flip 7 on iPhone and iPad. Tap cards to tally rounds and bonuses, check round history, undo mistakes, and pick up where you left off.
features: Round history and undo
Saves games locally on your device
Post-game stats
iPhone and iPad layouts

title: Spotify DJ
blurb: An older experiment that orders Spotify playlists by BPM, key, and danceability.
overview: Pulls audio features from Spotify and suggests a track order based on BPM, key, danceability, and energy. It's an older project, so check the repo setup notes before running it.
features: Audio feature analysis
Song-ordering algorithm
Playlist and track-library support
Configurable weighting

title: Physical Computing Final
blurb: A college physical computing project: a plastic garden owl rigged with a Pi camera, mic, and light sensor.
overview: Built for DIG333 at Davidson. A fake garden owl watches a walkway with a Raspberry Pi camera, microphone, and light sensor to count foot traffic, track noise levels, spot average shirt colors, and tweet updates about how busy it is.
features: Pi camera with OpenCV people counting
Microphone for walkway noise levels
Light sensor to put the owl to sleep at night
Automated status tweets from the owl

title: ComicScanner
blurb: My first take on a comic cataloging tool, using barcode scanning and image matching.
overview: An earlier Flask app for cataloging comics with barcode scanning, cover matching, metadata lookup, and collection import and export.
features: Barcode scanning
Cover image matching
Metadata lookup
Collection import and export

title: RSS News Summarizer
blurb: A small web app experiment that pulls RSS feeds and writes short summaries.
overview: Parses RSS feeds from multiple sources and generates short markdown summaries in a simple web UI.
features: RSS feed parsing
Multi-source aggregation
Automatic summaries
Markdown output

title: Spotify Preference Analyst
blurb: An older Python project that uses Spotify audio features and Euclidean distance to map out music taste.
overview: Uses linear algebra (Euclidean distance on Spotify's audio features) to analyze listening history, chart genres, and experiment with track recommendations.
features: Listening history analysis
Preference mapping with Euclidean distance
Genre charts
Recommendation experiments

title: earcandy
blurb: Drop in a finished electronic track to pull out each distinct sound as its own stem, plus a matching Serum 2 patch.
overview: A local macOS tool that splits a song into sound families (plucks, basses, leads, chops, risers, drum hits), exports each one as a stem, and searches Serum 2's factory presets for a matching patch. Separation runs locally on Apple silicon.
features: One stem and one .SerumPreset per sound
A/B playback of the mix, the isolated sound, and the Serum patch
Timeline showing every spot each sound appears
Refine, hide, and merge sound families

title: OMP Serve
blurb: A small browser workspace for coding-agent sessions running on my own server.
overview: A single-user web client for OMP agent sessions running on my own server. The agent, files, and shell commands stay on the server, and the browser just connects over a private network with no extra middleware or copies of the conversation.
features: Pick a project and model, then start or resume a conversation
Scratch conversations outside any project
Git changes view for workspaces

title: Tempo
blurb: An offline iPhone app for tracking food, workouts, and sleep, without streaks or scores.
overview: An iPhone app built around four tabs: Today, Eat, Move, and Sleep. No streaks, daily grades, or confetti. Optional AI planning goes through a server broker so no API keys ship in the app.
features: Barcode, nutrition label, and menu scanning for fast meal logging
Bodyweight, walking, and gym workouts with plain-English form cues
Workout Live Activity and Home Screen widgets
Apple Health import for sleep and body measurements

title: angl-dj
blurb: A self-hosted DJ tool for managing my music library, planning sets, and syncing with Rekordbox.
overview: Still early. Built with a FastAPI backend, background worker, React frontend, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Qdrant vector search. So far it has sign-in, a library dashboard, and health checks.
features: Library dashboard for audio files, recordings, analyzed tracks, and crates
Health checks for the database, queue, and vector search

title: py-trading
blurb: An experimental Python ML trading project with return forecasting, risk limits, and paper trading.
overview: Forecasts returns across multiple time horizons and turns them into portfolio weights, using point-in-time market data in DuckDB and Parquet so backtests don't cheat with future data. Strictly an experiment, not investment advice.
features: Point-in-time, as-of data queries
Risk limits with sector tilts and a drawdown throttle
Daily paper-trading loop with a dry-run mode

title: ANGL Comic Scanner
blurb: Point an iPhone at a comic cover to identify the series and issue, on-device and offline.
overview: The follow-up to my earlier comic scanner. A Python script packs a CLZ Comics export into a compressed bundle of cover thumbnails and image features, and the iOS app matches live camera frames on-device using Apple Vision first and OpenCV to double-check.
features: Runs completely on the phone with no network needed
Apple Vision search plus A-KAZE and RANSAC verification
Collection bundles built from a CLZ Comics export

title: Music
blurb: I make music too. My tracks are on SoundCloud.
overview: Original tracks and experiments, published on SoundCloud as tux.

title: JustBobThoughts
blurb: A Twitter bot that posted clips of the quiet, ambient moments from Bob Ross's painting shows.
overview: A weekend Python bot built on Tweepy that uploaded short clips of the ambient sections of Bob Ross's episodes to Twitter.
